items.title: Roscoe Mitchell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2023
items.q: I think I was pretty good at imitating like Nat King Cole and different people.

ctx.x: Well in a way I was. I mean I would say that like the art is on my mother’s side of the family. My uncle Charles Commodore Carter was an artist, and he had put together — what he worked with was crayon and he would layer the crayon and then he had a metal

protractor that he’d scrape and to blend the colors. And he did a book about my sisters and myself and our friends, and we were these people from outer space and so on. So the problem with that whole thing was you know he had moved out of our house and into the church, where he was also another pastor in there, and you know when he passed away those books are gone. And I’ve done everything you know, to try to find them and I can’t find them. But I mean they were glorious. But so the art comes from that side of…
Was there moments of, “All right, Roscoe, come and listen to this.” Did he have people that he chose for you to hear back then?
